added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite fields, both of which record failure_count 0 and failure_ids []; caveat: both fields name the same log (gate-importers-perfile.log), whose header names the base revision yet which contains tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py, a file absent at that revision, so the base arm is really a head run and the delta of 0 rests on that single head run rather than on two distinct arms.

findings.text: follow-on: the module docstring opens "Section 3 of *a-follower-row-is-worth-a-wake*", leaking the plan-document name and its section label into source, which the naming rule forbids in docstrings; the sibling follower test tests/test_follower_prints_only_policy_rows.py describes its mechanism without naming a plan, so this is unique among the tests here. Rewrite the paragraph to state the guarantee in mechanism terms (deliver a change that asks the coordinator for action and any reversal of a shown action row; hold a start, a bare re-announcement and a terminal echo) and drop the plan reference.

follow-on: baseline_suite.log_path and after_suite.log_path both name gate-importers-perfile.log (revision field 2e8c6fa vs 778219ba2), but that log's header reads "# revision: 2e8c6fa..." and it lists tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py, which does not exist at 2e8c6fa; the log is therefore a head run mislabelled as the base arm, so the base arm of the importer suite is not actually evidenced and the added-failure delta cannot be taken against a real base.

The manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite name the same log (gate-importers-perfile.log), whose header names the base revision yet which contains tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py, a file absent at that revision, so the base arm is not independently evidenced and the added-failure count rests on that single head run.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the follower delivers through section 1's row policy and its docstring states the guarantee; at head 778219ba2 reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2247-2256 rewrites the crew_follow docstring to state that a change asking the coordinator for action, or reversing a shown action row, prints while a start, a bare re-announcement and a terminal echo are held, and names the producer's log as the full stream, and tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py proves the two-row delivery against the real follower generator (cli._follow_watch_lines).
item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed manifest reads complete - status complete, the goal, the head gate, the two-arm importer fields, the negative control, commits, changed paths and a landing line - but its baseline_suite.log_path and after_suite.log_path are the same gate-importers-perfile.log and that log's own header names the base revision while the log contains a head-only test file, so the two arms are not two measurements.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the dispatch fenced the node to reckon/crew_follow_commands.py, tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py, a docs/evidence fragment and a docs/figures directory; git diff --name-only 2e8c6fa 778219ba2 lists exactly the production module, the new test and the evidence fragment, all inside the declared scope.

justifications.durability: the declared negative control - building the follower's row path with observer context shown - is executed and logged and I reproduced it in a scratch tree, reddening the two-row assertion and the settle-window assertion (2 failed EXIT=1), so the hold is shown to be load-bearing rather than a follower that reads nothing; tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py also carries a permanent observer-shown guard (test_observer_context_shown_delivers_the_start_rows_too); docked only because the mutation is applied to the source and the permanent guard patches the same class, so the two paths are one mechanism.
justifications.evidence: the head gate is recorded and reproduced (gate-head.log 3 passed EXIT=0; review-head-gate.log 3 passed EXIT=0 at 778219ba2) and the negative control is recorded and reproduced (negative-control.log 2 failed EXIT=1; review-nc-clean.log 2 failed EXIT=1); docked because the manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite name one and the same log, gate-importers-perfile.log, whose header names the base revision while containing a test file absent at that revision, so the base arm is not independently evidenced and the added-failure count of 0 is taken from a single head run rather than a genuine delta.
justifications.fit: the production change is a docstring paragraph whose wording follows the module's own prose idiom with no plan, stage, ticket or author label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the docstring in reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2247-2256 states section 1's guarantee and names the producer's log as the full stream; tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py drives the real follower (cli._follow_watch_lines) over dispatched->working->complete->recorded and working->exited-unfinished->blocked two seconds apart, asserts exactly the complete and the blocked rows reach the pane, and asserts the completion is released within [SETTLE_WINDOW, SETTLE_WINDOW+POLL] of the feed; docked because the fixture completion is followed by a recorded echo, so "a completion with no later transition" is shown via the echo being non-superseding rather than a literally transition-free completion.
justifications.reuse: tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py repeats the follower harness (home, _write_pointer, _live_runs, _event, _iso, _append_stream, _FLEET_EVENTS, observer_pane) almost verbatim from tests/test_follower_prints_only_policy_rows.py; repeating _write_pointer is the established idiom (69 test files define it), so the dock is mild, but observer_pane now exists in exactly two files and the shared harness could have been lifted to a helper; the genuinely new parts - the injected _Clock and the clock-timed _arm - are the reason the test exists and are not duplicated.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 2e8c6fa 778219ba2 lists exactly reckon/crew_follow_commands.py, tests/test_follow_settled_rows.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-follower-row-is-worth-a-wake/follower-delivers-settled-rows.html, all inside the dispatch's declared write paths, with no other file touched and a clean worktree at head.
